items.title: Crombie Says Beating Ford Would've Been 'Great for Mississauga' as Old Rivalry With Parrish Resurfaces
items.summary: According to Insauga, Thursday night's second Mississauga mayoral debate turned personal as Mayor Carolyn Parrish and her predecessor Bonnie Crombie traded sharp jabs, reviving a rivalry that dates back to a 2011 city council race between the two. City councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla also took part in the 90-minute debate, hosted by Food Banks Mississauga and the Metamorphosis Network at the food bank's east-end warehouse. Parrish, who won a mayoral byelection in June 2024 after Crombie left to lead the Ontario Liberals, questioned her rival's motives for wanting the job back. Crombie told Insauga it would have been "great for Mississauga" had she defeated Premier Doug Ford in the February 2025 provincial election, framing her failed run for the top job as something she pursued on the city's behalf. Much of the debate saw the two trade criticism over who would be more dedicated to serving as mayor, with Tedjo and Damerla also weighing in on the issues raised. The event marked the second of the campaign's mayoral debates as the Oct. 26 municipal election approaches.

items.title: Mississauga Man Held in Custody Nearly a Year After Puslinch Township Shooting
items.summary: According to Insauga, Ontario Provincial Police have charged a Mississauga man and two others with attempted murder in connection with a shooting that happened nearly a year ago in Puslinch Township, south of Guelph. Police say someone was shot in the early morning hours of Nov. 16, 2025, during what investigators describe as a home invasion, and the victim was taken to a trauma centre and later recovered. Two suspects were arrested in June, and a third was taken into custody on Sept. 9 as the investigation continued. OPP identified the Mississauga suspect as 20-year-old Lavontae Bowleg, who faces attempted murder with a restricted or prohibited firearm along with conspiracy, discharge of a firearm with intent, breaking and entering, and possession of property obtained by crime over $5,000. Bowleg remains in custody and is due in Guelph court on Oct. 9. An 18-year-old co-accused from Oshawa, who was a youth at the time of the shooting and cannot be named under the law, faces a similar set of charges. Police did not say in the release what led investigators to connect the three suspects to the shooting.

items.title: Affordability Tops List of Voter Concerns as Mississauga Residents Push Back on Tax Hikes
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, affordability has become the top concern among local voters heading into the Oct. 26 municipal election, with an August 2026 Liaison Strategies poll putting it at 19 per cent, ahead of taxes at 17 per cent and housing at 16 per cent. The outlet reports that when residents were asked how the city should respond to rising costs, 41 per cent said Mississauga should not raise taxes even if it means cutting services. Mary Simpson, president of the Town of Port Credit Association, says property taxes are shaping how many residents experience affordability pressures in the city. Simpson told the outlet that the issue came up repeatedly when association members met this past July, with one man in his 60s saying he felt priced out of his own home and unsure how much longer he could stay in Mississauga. The report ties the affordability debate to broader economic pressures, including the effects of U.S. tariffs, and notes some residents are calling for measures such as property tax deferrals. Candidates in the municipal race are being pressed on how they would balance keeping taxes low against maintaining city services and infrastructure as the vote approaches.

items.title: City Urges Caution as Shorter Days Raise Pedestrian Risk During October Safety Campaign
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, October marks both Pedestrian Safety Month and International Walk to School Month, and the city is using the campaign to remind road users to stay alert as daylight hours shrink. City officials say reduced visibility after dark raises the risk of collisions, particularly for pedestrians, cyclists and e-scooter riders, who face a higher chance of serious injury if struck. The city is encouraging students and families to keep walking, cycling or rolling to school through the fall, pointing to its School Walking Routes program, which uses signage around neighbourhoods to guide students and alert drivers to watch for children. Officials are asking everyone outdoors to dress appropriately for the colder weather and to stay visible as the days get shorter. The campaign ties into the city's broader road safety goal of eliminating fatalities and serious injuries from collisions on Mississauga's roadways. The city says the reminders apply to all road users, not just pedestrians, as drivers adjust to changing seasonal conditions.

items.title: Parrish's 'Blonde Bombshell' Jab at Crombie Sparks Backlash After Chaotic Mayoral Debate
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, Mississauga's four mayoral candidates admitted their Thursday night debate got "out of control," with exchanges that often turned more personal than policy-focused. Incumbent Carolyn Parrish faced off against former mayor Bonnie Crombie and city councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla at Food Banks Mississauga's headquarters, in a debate broadcast by CityNews and moderated by reporter Mark McAllister. The Star reports that Crombie called a Parrish jab referencing the return of the "blonde bombshell" to city hall demeaning, and said it reflected an increasingly mean-spirited campaign. Parrish responded that she felt she had to defend herself after Crombie accused her of never leaving her desk, saying she was yelling at everybody else and she had to get a word in as well. Both candidates agreed afterward that the debate had gotten out of control at points. The four sparred across a wide range of subjects, including police budgets and housing policy, with the tone growing more pointed as the night went on.

items.title: Builders Who Funded Parrish's Campaign Later Won Seats on Her Housing Task Force
items.summary: According to The Pointer, Mississauga Mayor Carolyn Parrish created a Housing Task Force shortly after winning the 2024 mayoral by-election that followed Bonnie Crombie's departure to lead the Ontario Liberal Party. Parrish had campaigned on making housing more affordable, and the task force was meant to cut the red tape developers face so homes could get built faster. The Pointer's review of Parrish's campaign finance disclosures found that several developers who later sat on that task force had also donated to her election campaign, within the province's $1,200 per-person contribution limit. The family behind TACC Developments, the DeGasperis family, appears three times on her donor list under that company name, the outlet reports. Kaneff Development, a longtime force in Mississauga's residential construction scene, donated through nine separate individuals totalling $10,800 before later being added to Parrish's roster of task force developers. The Pointer frames the overlap as part of a broader question about who will ultimately cover the city's multi-billion-dollar infrastructure funding gap as development fees continue to be reduced.

items.title: Parrish, Crombie, Tedjo and Damerla Trade Barbs in 90-Minute CityNews Mayoral Showdown
items.summary: According to CityNews, Mississauga's four leading mayoral candidates faced off Thursday night in a 90-minute debate moderated by CityNews' Mark McAllister that produced heated exchanges, personal jabs and what the outlet called a few mic-drop moments. The matchup pitted incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish and former three-term mayor Bonnie Crombie against city councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla, both of whom argued Mississauga is ready for new leadership. CityNews reports each candidate was asked a question before the floor opened to broader debate, a format that let the four repeatedly challenge each other's records directly. The outlet describes the tone as combative at points, with candidates working to distinguish themselves from the rest of the field while defending their own track records in municipal government. The debate covered several of the themes that have dominated the campaign so far, according to the outlet. The event came as Mississauga's mayoral race heads into its final stretch, with CityNews describing it as one of the more contentious debates of the campaign.
